ScopeAndLimitations.Method: Repository-wide static assessment of current application source/configuration, not a diff review; dependency inventory resolved using mvn dependency:tree without a build/test run.
ScopeAndLimitations.Reviewed: All 10 production Java classes, upload.js, three Thymeleaf template output contexts, both production property profiles, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, all four Oracle initialization files, .env.example and credential/security references in tracked top-level documentation. Test configuration and existing test were read for context, not treated as production secrets.
ScopeAndLimitations.DependencyScope: 104 unique resolved direct and transitive Maven coordinates across compile/runtime/test scopes (11 direct). This security skill intentionally expands the core direct-only CVE setting; per-finding scope/origin is retained. Runtime scope inferred from Maven is not proof that a jar is packaged/deployed.
ScopeAndLimitations.AdvisorySource: GitHub global Security Advisories HTTPS API; 4 batches of at most 30 coordinates, pagination supported, no failed batches, withdrawn advisories excluded; 85 deduplicated range matches. Exact dependency versions are compared to affected ranges; no attack/reachability verification.
ScopeAndLimitations.CweScope: 59 requested rules in six categories. One confirmed pattern per rule; other occurrences may exist. RulesPassed is a compatibility name for NOT_FOUND rules, not a security certification. The checklist files retain bounded negative evidence; wrapper-format NOT_FOUND evidence is empty as required by their schemas.
ScopeAndLimitations.Excluded: Git history, ignored/untracked local secrets, .github/agents, assessment/skill/generated artifacts, native/JVM/dependency internals, binary images, live cloud/deployment infrastructure and container/base-image advisories were not audited. These results do not cover every possible CWE (for example CSRF/TLS outside the requested rule set).
ScopeAndLimitations.Validation: No source remediation, test execution, application build, attack traffic, live credential validation, staging or commits. Assessment JSON/schema/count/path consistency is checked separately.
ScopeAndLimitations.Secrets: No secret values or credential payloads are reproduced. Environment variable names, public usernames and synthetic test/example placeholders are not production credential findings.
ScopeAndLimitations.Confidence: High confidence in cited static source patterns and advisory coordinate matches; exploitability, deployment conditions and operational impact are not verified.

CweFindings.Name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.
CweFindings.Explanation: HomeController.uploadPhotos iterates the complete caller-supplied files list and performs per-file database work without enforcing app.file-upload.max-files-per-upload=10. The configured count is never read in production Java. Multipart total bytes are limited to 50MB, so the loop is not literally unbounded, but that byte cap does not enforce the intended ten-file limit and permits many small files and repeated database/image-processing operations. Upload authentication is required; excessive processing beyond the intended count is the confirmed pattern, not a measured service outage.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Initialization
CweFindings.Description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.
CweFindings.Explanation: Both normal and Docker profiles initialize the persistent Oracle schema using spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=create. Hibernate create recreates mapped tables on startup rather than retaining the existing photo data; docker-compose persists the Oracle data volume, so a routine application restart can destructively reinitialize previously stored gallery contents. This is configuration-level destructive resource initialization; actual database loss was not induced during this assessment.

CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: The public GET / handler calls getAllPhotos, which materializes all photo rows including photo_data into List<Photo>. Photo.photoData is an eager-by-default @Lob byte[] and the native SELECT explicitly includes every BLOB without pagination or a row/aggregate-byte cap. Total allocation therefore scales with the accumulated uploaded gallery size, not the per-file 10MB limit. With the documented 512MB heap, a sufficiently large gallery can cause substantial heap pressure on an unauthenticated request; repeated/concurrent requests compound it. No heap-exhaustion attack or production failure was executed.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto logs the deleted photo ID and DetailController repeats the ID/success result, but neither records the authenticated principal or a request/correlation identifier. Upload success/rejection logs likewise omit the actor. SecurityConfig enables HTTP Basic without an application security-audit listener or explicit authentication-event logging. The confirmed gap is missing actor attribution for destructive operations, not complete absence of logging. Upstream proxy/SIEM/runtime audit controls were not available for inspection.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.uploadPhoto accepts the client-supplied Content-Type allowlist but does not reject bytes when ImageIO finds no reader (lines 124-143), and non-IO image inspection exceptions continue (149-152). The original bytes and supplied MIME type are then persisted (154-166) and publicly served by PhotoFileController. An authenticated uploader can therefore store arbitrary non-image data by claiming an allowed image MIME type. This is a confirmed fail-open upload-type check; executable server-side upload, browser script execution from these bytes, and decoder exploitation are not demonstrated.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: In upload.js, file.name reaches errors (73) and showErrors.innerHTML (216-218) without HTML encoding. The original multipart filename also flows through HomeController.uploadPhotos into createPhotoCard HTML text/attributes (185-189), then insertAdjacentHTML (157). A specially named selected/dropped file can introduce executable markup into the uploading user browser. The error path occurs before authentication/network submission. The successful-upload path requires an authenticated upload. Server-rendered galleries use escaping Thymeleaf attributes/th:text; cross-user persistent XSS on a normal gallery reload is not established.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Oracle initialization scripts interpolate APP_USER/APP_USER_UPPER and APP_USER_PASSWORD directly into an unquoted shell here-document containing PL/SQL string literals and EXECUTE IMMEDIATE statements (01-create-user.sh:25-28; create-user.sh:27-30). These externally supplied environment values are not escaped for the SQL string-literal/identifier contexts. Quote-bearing values can alter or break SQL executed as SYSTEM. This is an unsafe deployment-time SQL construction pattern, not a demonstrated HTTP injection: control of startup environment configuration is a prerequisite. No credential values or exploit payloads are reproduced.

CategoryAssessments.Finding: Assessed 16 CWE rules in Code Quality: 3 FOUND, 13 NOT_FOUND
Evidence: Reviewed all production Java and JavaScript, templates, application profiles, Docker configuration and Oracle scripts. Local variables are initialized, nullable photo metadata is guarded before display, image pixel multiplication casts operands to long, JPA access stays in PhotoRepository, and ImageInputStream/ImageReader are closed/disposed. No confirmed obsolete API, malformed-length trust, incorrect numeric conversion/calculation, precedence error, constant-condition defect, leaked file handle, or infinite loop was found in repository-owned application code. Static source review does not certify dependency internals.
NOT_FOUND means no confirmed applicable source pattern, not proof of absence.

CategoryAssessments.Finding: Assessed 6 CWE rules in Concurrency & Synchronization: 0 FOUND, 6 NOT_FOUND
Evidence: Reviewed all production Java classes, upload.js event callbacks and Oracle startup scripts. Spring singleton controllers/services retain injected final dependencies and read-only configuration rather than mutable per-request fields; PhotoServiceImpl request state, ImageReader and ImageInputStream are local variables. Database mutation methods use Spring @Transactional and UUID IDs. No custom threads/executors, shared mutable static application collection, manual double-checked singleton construction, wait/notify, explicit lock acquisition or incorrectly synchronized code was found. Concurrent delete conflicts may return an error but do not establish a security-relevant race. Oracle create-if-absent scripts are not shown to execute concurrently by the supplied deployment. Database isolation and multi-instance races were not tested; absence of synchronized keywords alone is not treated as a defect.
NOT_FOUND is bounded by source review and is not proof of race freedom.

CategoryAssessments.Finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
Evidence: Reviewed SecurityConfig, application profiles, docker-compose, Dockerfile, Oracle initialization scripts, .env.example and tracked documentation. Production database/admin passwords are required environment inputs; BCrypt is used for the in-memory admin hash. Fixed usernames are identifiers, not secret credentials. Example placeholders and explicitly test-only H2/admin settings are not treated as deployed secrets. No embedded production password, immutable cryptographic key, private key or verified API token was identified in reviewed text. Gallery reads are explicitly public by design, mutation routes require authentication, and Oracle grants are schema-scoped; no confirmed permission-assignment defect under these five rules was established. Git history, actual environment values, container image contents and deployed permissions were not scanned. All secret-like values are withheld from assessment evidence.
NOT_FOUND does not certify that the repository/history or deployment contains no secrets.

CategoryAssessments.Finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in File & Path Security: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
Evidence: Reviewed all production Java controllers/services/repository/model, image processing, configuration, Oracle startup scripts, and client templates/JavaScript. Uploads are persisted as database byte arrays; route IDs go to JPA rather than filesystem paths. No application XML parser or request-derived filesystem path construction was found. Static review only; dependency/native XML behavior is outside these source-rule conclusions.
NOT_FOUND means no confirmed source pattern was identified within this scope, not proof of absence.

CategoryAssessments.Finding: Assessed 12 CWE rules in Injection Attacks: 2 FOUND, 10 NOT_FOUND
Evidence: Reviewed production Java/JavaScript, all templates, Oracle initialization scripts, Docker entrypoint and properties. PhotoRepository native SQL uses fixed query strings with @Param bindings; ID lookups use JpaRepository.
